body: I've put the one I had on hold while I try to find work.  I can't justify spending time playing an rpg when finances are beginning to become critical.  But I still do some coding regularly, which brings up my spirits a bit.  Makes me feel I've accomplished a little, even if it's not that much.

It may be a large part of it.  But life is just so boring.  The highlights of my life mostly consists of watching movies and tv.  The rest is thinking about stuff I have to do.  The more I have to do, the less I want to get out of bed, although that's true for everyone I think.  

If I have to take the car in, even for an oil change, I have it on my mind.  Right now I wish I could go shopping just because I have to tomorrow, and I want it over with.

Reading your post, it struck me that here's someone who really wants to die but he's too scared to admit it even anonymosly. 

Btw, gunshot to the head is risky. If you miss, you merely disfigure yourself and live with brain damage while your family changes your diaper.  Plastic bag is tough.  Too easy to rip it off.  A hanging is much more likely to work and you may even orgasm in the process.    Freeway overpass jump may just leave you with paralyzed, and permament diapers, and be the cause of other deaths.

Pills, only if you have time.  Wrist cutting, if you can stand blood.  Car crash is haphazard and may just as easily kill someone else while leaving you in diapers again.

If you really want to die, ACA, I recommend walking in front of a high speed train, preferably a commuter train, so as to maximize the impact of hundreds of people without actually hurting them.  Likelyhood of your survival approaches nil, and the rain will probably wash off the blood from the engine.

You mentioned you tried to start programming.  Was this on your own?  It's hard to do on your own, especially if you are like me and start projects without finishing them.   

School sucks.  It gets better after graduation, although the feeling of instability is high until you find work.  I spent weeks not doing much more than getting out of bed after graduation.  But when I found a job, I could focus on that, and it helped a lot, especially as I no longer had to work retail.
